content:
Devon: Heads up — seeing a wave of pod evictions on gpu-pool nodes in us-east-1a. Kubelet setting NetworkUnavailable and evicting pods even though simple pings between nodes look fine.

sre-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: INC-2025-214 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2025-214) — paging @oncall-eng

Priya: Which nodes? can you paste a kubelet log snippet from one of the affected nodes?

Devon: node-gn02-us-east-1a-03 is noisy. here's the relevant kubelet segment — I trimmed it: 

```
May 18 03:12:21 node-gn02 kubelet[1234]: I0518 03:12:21.123456 1234 cni.go:289] Network plugin status: adding pod sandbox for pod "gpu-train-0"
May 18 03:12:21 node-gn02 kubelet[1234]: E0518 03:12:21.123789 1234 cni.go:312] Network plugin failed: failed to setup pod networking: set network unavailable: failed to add route: write udp: no buffer space available
May 18 03:12:21 node-gn02 kubelet[1234]: I0518 03:12:21.124000 1234 kubelet_node_status.go:123] Setting NodeCondition NetworkUnavailable=True
May 18 03:12:21 node-gn02 kubelet[1234]: I0518 03:12:21.125000 1234 eviction_manager.go:345] Evicting pod "gpu-train-0" due to node condition NetworkUnavailable
```

Ben: "no buffer space" screams conntrack / skbuff exhaustion or MTU causing fragmentation. Did we push any kernel or NIC driver updates in the maintenance window?

Clara: We rolled a kernel update to the cos image on the GPU fleet last night and also flipped the host NICs to Jumbo MTU 9000 for RDMA perf. CNI overlay (vxlan/flannel) default MTU is still 1450. Could be fragmentation causing the CNI to fail intermittently.

Priya: Can you show `ip link` and `ethtool` output? also `dmesg` for skb/conntrack drops.

Devon: pasted outputs from node-gn02-us-east-1a-03:

```
# ip link show | egrep -i "eth|flannel|vxlan"
2: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
4: flannel.1: mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default
7: vxlan0: mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UP mode DEFAULT group default

# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count=1294300
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1310720

# dmesg | tail -n 6
[  542.123456] skb: queue memory limit exceeded: dropping packet
[  542.123457] nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
```

Ben: yep — conntrack filling + MTU mismatch between host (9000) and overlay (1450) -> fragmentation and kernel skb pressure. For RDMA-enabled NICs we set host MTU 9000 but didn't adjust CNI vxlan to use host-gw or configure jumbo-safe MTU.

Clara: Impact path: CNI tries to program routes, large packets are being dropped on host due to LRO/GRO or skbuff shortage, CNI fails to set up sandbox and kubelet flips NetworkUnavailable -> eviction. So it's a false positive from kubelet perspective but triggered by underlying MTU/conntrack resource exhaustion.

Priya: Short-term mitigation ideas: 
- bump nf_conntrack_max on affected nodes (we already increased it on node above, but it's cluster-wide)
- restart kube-proxy / calico/flannel DaemonSet on the pool to force reprogramming with correct MTU
- add a short kubelet tolerance so we avoid mass evictions while we patch CNI (increase NodeStatusUpdateFrequency / node-status lease?)

Devon: For the immediate blast radius reduction I patched a host-level sysctl DaemonSet to increase nf_conntrack_max and applied a rolling restart to flannel on gpu nodes. Evictions dropped but not zero.

Priya: For a safer kubelet-level mitigation, we can increase lease duration so the control plane won't mark nodes NotReady quickly. There's a kube-controller-manager flag `--node-lease-duration-seconds` (default 40s) and kubelet has NodeStatus frequency settings via KubeletConfig. We can request a short bump for the pool in the next maintenance change to 120s while we fix CNI.

Ben: Long term: standardize host MTU across stack: either set host to 1500 for overlay usage, or use host-gw/SR-IOV passthrough for RDMA nodes and configure CNI to honor 9000. Also tune conntrack provisioning for gpu-heavy workloads (high ephemeral connections).

Clara: Filing follow-ups: INC-2025-214 has the plan: 
- revert host MTU on non-RDMA nodes to 1500 where overlay used 
- update CNI configs for RDMA nodes to use non-overlay networking or adjust VXLAN MTU to 8970+
- add automated check to alert when host MTU != CNI MTU for future upgrades

Devon: Current status: evictions reduced ~85% after nf_conntrack bump + flannel restart. Still monitoring. Will keep this thread updated.

Priya: Thanks — once stabilized let's add a runbook entry for MTU+kubelet false-negative evictions so oncall can triage faster next time. :+1:

sre-bot: Incident INC-2025-214 status: monitoring -> mitigated.
